title: CUDA ABI/runtime drift — init OOM sleuth
content:
Goal: capture a short, messy timeline + commands and hypotheses while reproducing an intermittent init OOM that looks correlated with driver/CUDA ABI mismatch. Keep quick notes so I can hand to SRE or pair with someone later.

Summary of problem:
- Some nodes (k8s dev pool) see Python processes fail during model init with "CUDA error: out of memory" or low-level cublas/driver errors immediately at first allocation. Happens after recent node image update (kernel + driver bump) and container base image still using cuda 12.2 runtime libs. Symptoms: OOM-like message but total free GPU memory seems sufficient; dmesg shows driver complaints on some boots.

Repro steps (what I ran locally on a repro node):
1) basic system checks
$ hostname && date
repro-node-13 2026-03-12T20:05:02Z

$ nvidia-smi -q | head -n 40
Driver Version                          : 535.113.01
CUDA Version                            : 12.3
Attached GPUs                           : 1
FB Memory Usage                         : 12066 MiB / 24576 MiB

$ dpkg -l | egrep 'nvidia|cuda' || rpm -qa | egrep 'nvidia|cuda'
ii  nvidia-driver-535  535.113.01-0ubuntu1
ii  cuda-toolkit-12-3  12.3.1-1

2) container runtime info (we run ubuntu:22.04 + cudnn/cuda libs via image tag)
$ docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint bash redwood/runtime:cuda-12.2-2026-02-15 -c 'ldconfig -p | egrep "libcuda|libcublas"'
libcuda.so.1 (libc6,x86-64) => /usr/local/nvidia/lib64/libcuda.so.1
libcublas.so.12 (libc6,x86-64) => /usr/local/cuda-12.2/targets/x86_64-linux/lib/libcublas.so.12

Observations: container has CUDA 12.2 libs while host driver is 535 (CUDA 12.3). In theory compatible but not guaranteed with newer driver ABI changes.

3) quick program reproducer (PyTorch)
# minimal.py
import torch
print(torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available())
a = torch.randn((8000, 8000), device='cuda')
print('alloc done')

Run inside container
$ python minimal.py
12.2 True
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'c10::Error'
  what():  CUDA error: out of memory at ../aten/src/ATen/cuda/CUDACachingAllocator.cpp:xxx
Aborted (core dumped)

But nvidia-smi showed plenty of free memory before run.

4) check low-level error traces from python + libcuda:
- run with LD_DEBUG=libs to see which libcuda is loaded (host->container interaction)
$ LD_DEBUG=libs python minimal.py 2>&1 | egrep 'libcuda|cublas' | sed -n '1,200p'
...
23456: find library=libcuda.so.1 [0]; searching
23456: search path=/usr/local/nvidia/lib64:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu; searching
23456: trying file=/usr/local/nvidia/lib64/libcuda.so.1

5) kernel/dmesg snippets captured after failed init (repro-node-13):
[Mar 12 20:04:59] NVRM: GPU at 00000000:01:00.0 has failed with an XID 86
[Mar 12 20:04:59] NVRM: Xid (86): GPU page fault, PDE/DMA map fail, probably caused by user process
[Mar 12 20:04:59] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.

Xid 86 + "GPU has fallen off the bus" is scary and points to driver/hw/PCI issue, not pure allocator. But it coincides with the host-driver bump and the container runtime mismatch.

6) ldd and SONAME checks inside container and on host (to look for symbol differences):
$ docker run --rm --gpus all redwood/runtime:cuda-12.2-2026-02-15 \
  bash -lc 'ldd /usr/local/nvidia/lib64/libcuda.so.1 | sed -n "1,80p"'
	libc.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6 (0x7f...)
	libm.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libm.so.6 (0x7f...)

$ nm -D /usr/local/nvidia/lib64/libcuda.so.1 | egrep 'cuMemAlloc|cuLaunchKernel' || true
00000000000 T cuMemAlloc_v2

Host libcuda symbolic check:
$ nm -D /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so | egrep 'cuMemAlloc_v2|cuMemAlloc' || true
00000000000 T cuMemAlloc_v2

So symbol exists on both; but versions/tables might differ.

Things tried so far (and outcomes):
- Reboot node -> sometimes clears. Repro is flaky (50/50).
- Downgraded host driver to 525 on one node: issue stopped reproducing on that node for ~24h.
- Switched container base to cuda:12.3-runtime tag -> reduced flakiness in local runs.
- Tried LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/nvidia/lib64/libcuda.so.1 inside container -> program crashed earlier (still OOM/XID).
- Exported CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 and reduced allocation size -> no crash (allocation fits) but crash occurs even for tiny tensors in one case (suggests driver fatal state).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Host driver (535) introduced a regression with some PCI/firmware combos that causes GPU to fall off bus when certain contexts are created. When container links mismatched runtime, shared memory or kernel interactions provoke bug. Evidence: dmesg XID86, node-specific, cleared by driver downgrade.
2) ABI mismatch between container's cuda 12.2 libs and host driver 12.3 -> subtle symbol table mismatch or behavior change leading to allocator attempts that the driver rejects (less likely because SONAME symbols match, but table layout could differ).
3) Kernel/PTE/hugepage interaction: large initial allocation triggers a DMA mapping path that fails with updated driver/firmware combination (fits XID PDE/DMA map fail message).
4) Container runtime mounting of /usr/local/nvidia and host lib paths causes stale libraries to be used by host processes (race in driver module vs container libs).

Data to collect next:
- exact cuda driver kernel module git tag / build id on failing node: cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version and modinfo nvidia
- capture full core dump and libbacktrace (gdb) of crashed process to see symbol addresses at time of abort.
- instrument small repro that does only cuInit + cuMemAlloc(1) and log return codes; run many iterations to see if first allocation or later one triggers XID.
- try repro with og host driver + container runtime pinned to exact same CUDA 12.3 runtime (verify if aligning runtime removes errors).
- collect ABI exports: readelf -s /usr/local/nvidia/lib64/libcuda.so.1 | egrep 'cuMemAlloc' and compare symbol version tags between host and container.

Quick commands to run on nodes (for SRE handoff):
- sudo modinfo nvidia | egrep 'version|srcversion'
- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
- journalctl -k -u kubelet --since "20 minutes ago" | egrep -i 'nvrm|xid|gpu' -n
- CUDA debug: set env CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 CUDA_DRIVER_DEBUG=1 and capture stdout/stderr (may flood logs).

Notes about triage approach:
- If XID appears in dmesg, escalate to infra-heavy debugging (driver upstream/firmware). XID with "GPU has fallen off the bus" is often hardware/PCI or driver crash, not just allocator.
- If errors are pure CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED but no kernel XID, focus on allocator caching and memory fragmentation; try setting PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHE=1 and test.
- Avoid mixing host and container libcuda versions by preferring container runtime image with compatible CUDA runtime matching host driver when possible. We should add an admission check in node-provisioning that warns on driver/runtime mismatch severity.

Scratch TODOs (short):
- [ ] Run repeated cuInit+cuMemAlloc(1) loop on repro node with driver 535 and with 525 to quantify failure rate.
- [ ] Collect /proc/driver/nvidia/version and full modinfo output for failing node and attach to INF-2412.
- [ ] Build small C repro (libcuda direct) to avoid PyTorch layers; log raw error codes and write timestamps to file.
- [ ] Add node-provisioning linter rule to check driver vs container runtime tags and warn when driver > container major/minor by >= 1.

Random notes / breadcrumbs:
- Saw a similar issue in internal slack thread #gpu-ha from 2025-11: user reported XID 86 after driver 535 upgrade; they resolved by downgrading driver to 520 temporarily while NVIDIA released a patch.
- On one node `nvidia-smi top` showed a zombie process had retained a context; killing it freed memory and stopped immediate crashes for a while. Might be a leak + driver regression combo.

If passing to SRE: include the logs/dmesg XID lines, node kernel version, modinfo output, container image tag, and a short repro which does only cuInit + small alloc loop. That should help NV support triage ABI vs driver bug.

End of scratchpad.
